claims.text: The target system is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi in both solid and liquid states.
The proposed method applies near the alloy melting temperature, defined as within approximately ±10% of Tm.
The conventional EAM reference in TOR-TILD should be replaced with a machine-learning interatomic potential.
The MLIP should be trained on a broad ab initio dataset containing both ordered solid and highly disordered liquid configurations.
An MLIP's many-body functional form and local atomic descriptors can represent the complex coordination environments of disordered liquids.
Training on diverse solid and liquid ab initio configurations will enable the MLIP to capture subtle local interactions and many-body effects.
Capturing these interactions will produce a more accurate mapping of the ab initio energy landscape.
A more accurate energy-landscape mapping will improve phase-space overlap between the reference potential and the ab initio target.
Improved reference-target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
MLIP-based TI free energies should converge to within roughly 5–10 meV/atom of full ab initio integration results.
Convergence within 5–10 meV/atom would be a substantial improvement over a traditional EAM reference.
Unmodified EAM references typically exhibit larger free-energy discrepancies because they sample the many liquid atomic configurations poorly.
The proposed approach may also apply to multicomponent alloy systems similar to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi near their melting temperatures.
Effectiveness for substantially different compositions or temperature regimes has not been established.
MLIP transferability to configurations outside the training distribution depends on training-set diversity and rigorous cross-validation.
The quantitative improvement will depend on the quality of the ab initio data and the MLIP training protocol.
